title: Netflix Buys Wu-Tang Clan Doc ‘The Disciple’ Directed by Joanna Natasegara (EXCLUSIVE)
description: “The Disciple: A Wu-Tang Fable” the Sundance-bowing doc that unravelled the story of Dutch-Moroccan rapper and producer Cilvaringz and the making of
body:
“The Disciple: A Wu-Tang Fable” the Sundance-bowing doc that unravelled the story of Dutch-Moroccan rapper and producer Cilvaringz and the making of the controversial Wu-Tang Clan record “Once Upon a Time in Shaolin,” is heading to Netflix. 

	The streamer has acquired rights to the feature, directed and produced by Oscar-winning British filmmaker Joanna Natasegara (“The White Helmets,” “The Edge of Democracy”) in her feature directorial debut, and has set a release date of Oct. 16.  
	

	Boasting the Wu-Tang’s own the RZA as an exec producer and contributor, “The Disciple” tells the wild tale of Tarik Azzougarh, better known by his stage name Cilvaringz. A Wu-Tang fanboy while in his teens in the the 90s, through relentless determination he managed to do the unthinkable and work his way into the group’s inner circle, touring the world with his heroes and being mentored along the way by the RZA himself. 


	But the film also charts how Cilvaringz’ “ambition and creativity” would converge to see him record “Once Upon a Time in Shaolin,” a 31-track record of which only copy was made and in 2015 was auctioned off to the highest bidder. “It’s scarcity is a form of protest, and an argument that music still holds intrinsic worth as art in a digital age,” reads the synopsis. “The result is one of the most controversial artifacts of our time that sparked ongoing conversations about technology, creation and ownership.”

	Unfortunately, the record’s highest bidder — who paid $2 million, making it the most expensive musical work ever sold — was notorious (and later convicted) entrepreneur Martin Shkreli, adding further controversy over the project.
	

	“For the last five years making this film has been a labour of love and discovery for me,” said Natasegara, who reunites with Netflix after her short film “The White Helmets” won the streamer its first Oscar in 2016. “Initially I was inspired by a teenhood love of Wu-Tang and a story about the secret album ‘Once Upon a Time in Shaolin’ too intriguing to miss. In the making I discovered so much more about why Tarik, myself, and so many of us idolise them. They stand for so much that is so needed right now — community, talent, tenacity, innovation and love. I’m so thrilled audiences will get to spend time in this world I’ve loved so much.”

	“The Disciple: A Wu-Tang Fable” is a Netflix Documentary in association with Studio Gebbia, Film4, 36 Cinema, Sony Music Vision; an Aluna Entertainment and Violet Films production. It was produced by Abigail Anketell-Jones, Lauren Dark and Vanessa Kirby. Executive producers include The RZA, Joe Gebbia, Jason Ropell, Abazar Khayami; David Kimbangi, Farhana Bhula and Ollie Madden for Film4; Trevor Burgess, Gary Hess and James Costa for Bird Street Productions. Editors were Chloë Lambourne and Chris Dickens.

schema.headline: Netflix Buys Wu-Tang Clan Doc ‘The Disciple’ Directed by Joanna Natasegara (EXCLUSIVE)

title: Box Office: ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ to Rule in Fourth Weekend, ‘Insidious: Out of the Further’ Aims for $25 Million Debut
description:
“Insidious: Out of the Further” won’t topple the box office reign of “Spider-Man: Brand New Day.”

	The sixth “Insidious” installment is targeting $
body:
“Insidious: Out of the Further” won’t topple the box office reign of “Spider-Man: Brand New Day.”

	The sixth “Insidious” installment is targeting $23 million to $27 million in its domestic debut, likely enough for second place on North American charts. “Brand New Day” should retain the No. 1 spot in its fourth weekend, with the superhero sequel estimated to earn $35 million to $40 million between Friday and Sunday. Both movies hail from Sony.
	

	Unless “Out of the Further” beats expectations, the latest “Insidious” won’t improve upon the start of its predecessor, 2023’s “The Red Door,” which opened to $33 million. However, the paranormal sequel cost just $18 million to produce, so it won’t require a huge turnout to reap box office rewards. This film serves as a sequel to “Insidious: The Red Door” and follows a new family as they explore the creepy concept of “the Further” — a purgatorial place inhabited by the tortured spirits of the dead.


	“Insidious” has been a commercially successful series, with the five low-budget films having generated a combined $740 million globally. The 2013 sequel “Insidious: Chapter 2” currently stands as the biggest debut in the franchise with $40 million, however “The Red Door” ranks as the highest-grossing entry to date with $189 million worldwide.

	This weekend also sees the release of Lionsgate’s action-thriller “Mutiny,” starring Jason Statham, as well as Black Bear’s comedy “Spa Weekend,” led by Isla Fisher, Leslie Mann, Anna Faris and Michelle Buteau. Neither film is expected to break out in its opening weekend.
	

	“Mutiny” is targeting a soft $8 million $10 million from 2,700 theaters. It cost $40 million to produce; Lionsgate acquired North American rights but didn’t finance the film. Statham plays a former marine who has to prove his innocence after he’s framed for murdering his billionaire boss. “Spa Weekend” is aiming for just $3 million to $5 million from 2,000 screens. It carries a roughly $20 million price tag. Directed by Jon Lucas and Scott Moore, the movie follows three burned-out childhood besties who travel to a luxury resort in Palm Springs.

	Those films are expected to land behind “The Odyssey,” which should bring in roughly $15 million in its sixth weekend of release. Christopher Nolan’s blockbuster is the second-biggest movie of the year with $504 million in North America and $1.29 billion worldwide to date.

	Meanwhile, “Spider-Man: Brand New Day” will continue its epic box office run. The Tom Holland-led Spidey adventure just crossed $800 million domestically after 19 days, the fastest film to hit the milestone and fourth movie ever to do so. With $804 million in North America and $2.078 billion globally to date, it’s already the sixth-highest grossing movie in history, trailing just 2009’s “Avatar” ($2.9 billion), 2019’s “Avengers: Endgame” ($2.7 billion), 2022’s “Avatar: The Way of Water” ($2.3 billion) and 1994’s “Titanic” ($2.2 billion) and ahead of 2015’s “Star Wars: The Force Awakens” ($2.07 billion) and 2018’s “Avengers: Infinity War” ($2.05 billion).

	This summer has been the biggest since the pandemic upended the industry, with revenues surpassing $4 billion for only the second time since COVID. Domestic ticket sales stand at $4.24 billion from May 1 through Aug. 16, running 23% ahead of the same period in 2025 and nearly 6% ahead of 2019. With two weekends to go before Labor Day, popcorn season could even eclipse the all-time summer record set in 2013 with $4.755 billion (not adjusted for inflation), according to Rentrak.

schema.headline: Box Office: ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ to Rule in Fourth Weekend, ‘Insidious: Out of the Further’ Aims for $25 Million Debut

title: ‘Building the Band’ Group Soulidified Signs to Atlantic Records (EXCLUSIVE)
description: Soulidified has signed to Atlantic Records, just a year after they were introduced to the world on Netflix’s “Building the Band,” Variety can exclus
body:
Soulidified has signed to Atlantic Records, just a year after they were introduced to the world on Netflix’s “Building the Band,” Variety can exclusively announce.

	The group, consisting of Shade Jenifer, Malik Heard, Bradley Rittmann and Landon Boyce, was initially formed on “Building the Band,” which aired in July 2025. They joined together as a quartet in episode three of the show and gave standout performances of Usher’s “U Remind Me” and Miguel’s “Sure Thing.”
	

	“We’re proud to officially call Atlantic home,” says Soulidified in a statement to Variety. “As a band blending backgrounds, our harmony stands for something bigger—unity that we’re excited to share with the world. We’ve worked hard to get here, and we know we’re just getting started. To our fans around the world, thank you for believing in us from day one. We love you more than words can say. Atlantic, let’s have some fun, we’ve got a whole world to take over.”


	Soulidified has been steadily grinding since their time on “Building the Band,” releasing their debut original single “One & Only” in August 2025 and their latest “What’s Your Name” this past February. The group recently supported Khalid on four of his shows and are currently plotting their “What’s Your Name” tour, which will touch down in Brazil, Amsterdam, Paris, Berlin and London this fall.

	“From the first time I saw them on ‘Building the Band,’ I knew these four had a rare quality I hadn’t seen in any group I’ve managed before,” says Soulidified’s manager Johnny Wright, an industry veteran who has steered the careers of Backstreet Boys and New Kids on the Block. Wright manages the group alongside Day to Day Management’s Fernando Watson and Jayvon Hicks. “Beyond their obvious vocal and performance talent,” continues Wright, “the fact that they came together sight unseen makes it clear God had a hand in their story. I’m proud to be part of their journey and especially excited that they are now a part of the Bee/Wright Entertainment, Atlantic Records, and WME family.”
	

	“We could not be more excited to welcome Soulidified to the Atlantic family,” adds Michael Parker, svp of A&R, and Justin Horowitz, vp of digital marketing, at Atlantic. “Beyond their undeniable talent, this band is breaking boundaries in ways that no band has before. What they represent and stand for, both individually and as a group, has already garnered an incredible community that we can’t wait to watch grow and evolve.”

title: Nielsen Makes New Bid to Capture ‘Co-Viewing’ as  TV Season Approaches
description:
Nielsen is really working the room.

	The media-measurement giant aims to measure viewers of video content more accurately and will place a focus on
body:
Nielsen is really working the room.

	The media-measurement giant aims to measure viewers of video content more accurately and will place a focus on capturing so-called “co-viewing,” or multiple viewers watching the same piece of programming together at the same location. The effort means TV executives may get more credit for shows that bring people together at parties and in bars, among other gathering places.


	 Nielsen will use new wearable measurement devices that resemble a smart watch that will be placed on the wrists of Nielsen panelists and capture audio from TV events, shows and movies, allowing for more passive measurement the company believes will create result in a more accurate picture of how many people are watching a given program.
	

	“We are relentless in our pursuit of delivering the most accurate measurement possible for our media and advertising clients,” said Karthik Rao, CEO of Nielsen, in a statement. “We’ve spent months working hand in hand with them and industry experts to make Big Data + Panel even more accurate.”

	Despite the rise of a swath of new competitors, Nielsen’s measurement remains the bedrock element of determining the size and other attributes of video audiences, and is a key element in data that helps underpin value and price in talks between advertisers and TV networks and streamers. Nielsen launched a “Big Data + Panel” product in early 2025 that could examine audience interactions with cable and satellite set-top boxes and smart TVs across 45 million households and 75 million devices.

	The company has faced some backlash, with the Video Advertising Bureau, an advocacy group that represents major video publishers and TV networks to the advertising industry, accusing Nielsen of releasing data that could be inconsistent.  
	

	The new tweaks aren’t being made without preparation. Nielsen has worked with many of its clients to prepare them for the changes, including sharing preview data with them, and negotiating timing of the updates with the Media Rating Council, an independent arbiter of ratings-measurement systems and technologies.

	In addition to the work to capture co-viewing, Nielsen has fixed timing delays in its use of data from the Advertising Research Foundation. It has combined data from two different surveys — the American Community Survey, which is conducted by the U.S. Census, and the National Hispanic Enumeration Survey– to better estimate audiences for Spanish-language content. And it is updating its methodology for measuring certain aspects of ACR data, which often comes from technology embedded in smart TVs.

schema.headline: Nielsen Makes New Bid to Capture ‘Co-Viewing’ as  TV Season Approaches

title: Julie Andrews to Narrate Jane Austen’s ‘Emma’ for Noiser Podcast Network (EXCLUSIVE)
description:
Dame Julie Andrews will continue to lend her dulcet tones to the world of Jane Austen. 

	The stage and screen icon — an Oscar, BAFTA and multi Emmy
body:
Dame Julie Andrews will continue to lend her dulcet tones to the world of Jane Austen. 

	The stage and screen icon — an Oscar, BAFTA and multi Emmy and Grammy award winner — will return for a second season of “Jane Austen Stories” to narrate “Emma” in its unabridged form. Told exactly how Austen’s wrote it, “Emma” will be released in serialised episodes from Aug. 25 by U.K. podcast network Noiser.


	Accompanied by original cinematic music and immersive sound design, the series will brings Austen’s words to life while remaining faithful to the author’s original text.
	

	First published in 1815, “Emma” is one of Austen’s most enduring and entertaining novels, following the confident, well-meaning Emma Woodhouse as her attempts at matchmaking lead her into a series of increasingly complicated misunderstandings. More than 200 years later, her wit, social observations and wonderfully flawed characters remain as captivating as ever.

	“Emma” — which will be told across 27 instalments — follows Noiser’s “Pride and Prejudice,” also narrated by Andrews, and the network’s “Sherlock Holmes Short Stories” series, narrated by Hugh Bonneville (“Paddington,” “Downton Abbey”), both of which have drawn millions of listeners worldwide. 

	Alongside the Noiser podcast series with Andrews, Austen’s novels are about to enjoy something of boom on screen. The feature adaptation of “Sense and Sensibility,” directed by Georgia Oakley and starring Daisy Edgar-Jones, Esmé Creed-Miles, Caitríona Balfe, Frank Dillane, George MacKay, and Fiona Shaw, is releasing on Sep. 25 with Focus. Meanwhile, Netflix’s series adaptation of “Pride and Prejudice,” directed by Euros Lyn and starring Emma Corrin, Jack Lowden, Olivia Colman, Rufus Sewell, Daryl McCormack and Louis Partridge, is due for release later in the year.

schema.headline: Julie Andrews to Narrate Jane Austen’s ‘Emma’ for Noiser Podcast Network (EXCLUSIVE)

title: ‘The End of Times’ Acquired by Split Screen Ahead of Venice Premiere (EXCLUSIVE)
description: Zagreb-based sales outlet Split Screen has secured international rights to “The End of Times” ahead of its world premiere in Critics’ Week, an indep
body:
Zagreb-based sales outlet Split Screen has secured international rights to “The End of Times” ahead of its world premiere in Critics’ Week, an independent sidebar to the Venice Film Festival.

	In Bibiana Rojas Gómez and Juan David Cárdenas Maldonado’s film, Salomé searches through five decades of family footage for the reasons for her mother’s sadness. Trying to imagine different versions of her mother, Salomé finds out that all of them lead to depression and uneasiness in a context where it seems easier to conceive the end of the world than the end of capitalism.
	

	By using Artificial Intelligence, she experiences in first person how difficult it is to conceive another version of the world, the one where her mother could find some kind of meaning.


	The directors said, “Our age has glorified technological utopia, and the latest version of this promise is artificial intelligence. Yet, like earlier technological novelties, the shine of progress is discreetly stained by ambition, exploitation and misery.”

	They added, “Seen from the perspective of peripheral countries condemned to the dark side of development and turned into an impoverished labor force, A.I. exposes its shadiest aspects.

	“Our film seeks to show how the achievements of civilization are also triumphs of barbarism – a barbarism that is currently the rule under contemporary capitalism, or neoliberalism, a system of generalized physical and emotional exhaustion. In these conditions, depression has become the most common disease, not merely as a psychiatric phenomenon but as a social response to current material, economic and political realities.
	

	“This project is an initiative to politicize mental illness. When it seems impossible to conceive a better world, sadness becomes the most usual form of adaptation.”

	Marcella Jelic and Lorena Morin from Screen Split said, “Bibiana’s and Juan’s work caught our attention very quickly. It builds a remarkably complex narrative, using minimal resources for it. Not only in an original, but catchy and at times haunting way, they seamlessly connect an intimate family trauma with the broader colonial history of Latin America. It is a film which undeniably leaves one reflecting on the current state of us as a society.”

	“The End of Times” is produced by Luis Esguerra Cifuentes (Bruma Cine, Colombia), co-produced by Bibiana Rojas Gómez (A Fuego Lento, Colombia) and Juan David Cárdenas Maldonado (Allegro Films, Colombia). Atomic Media Group served as the associate producer.

title: ‘Who Wants to Be a Millionaire’ Ends Summer Run With Consecutive Weeks of Ratings Growth
description: ABC recently decided to move some of this summer’s run of “Who Wants to Be a Millionaire” into the fall — and perhaps it doesn’t hurt that it’s doin
body:
ABC recently decided to move some of this summer’s run of “Who Wants to Be a Millionaire” into the fall — and perhaps it doesn’t hurt that it’s doing very well so far this season.

	“Millionaire,” hosted by Jimmy Kimmel, has now been the No. 1 primetime entertainment program with viewers for the third week in a row, growing every week since its season premiere on July 22. The show’s most recent episode, on Aug. 12, averaged 4.41 million viewers (up 2% from the previous week’s 4.33 million) according to Nielsen’s National Live+Same Day Big Data Plus Panel Program Ratings. 
	

	That repped the show’s best performance since last year’s July 30, 2025 episode where Matt Damon and Ken Jennings won $1 million. (That was the most-watched episode of “Millionaire” in five years — since 6.52 million on June 4, 2020 — during the first season that Kimmel took over as host.)


	It was also the most-watched show of the night, beating CBS’ “Big Brother” by 28% in total viewers, and also the week’s most-watched primetime entertainment program, beating NBC’s “America’s Got Talent” by 19%.

	Last week’s episode featured guest players Jesse Eisenberg and Paul Giamatti, and then Krysten Ritter and Sarah Shahi.

	Originally slated to run through the summer, “Who Wants to Be a Millionaire” will take a breather after this Wednesday night’s episode, which includes comedians Paul Scheer and Rob Huebel as a team, followed by actress and rapper Awkwafina and director Paul Feig. 

	The show will then take a hiatus, and return with the season’s final three episodes on three consecutive Wednesdays: Oct. 7, 14 and 21. (“Celebrity Jeopardy,” which was originally scheduled for the time slot, will air at a later date.)
	

	Among the highlights so far this season, Ben Affleck and “Jeopardy!” champion Jamie Ding won the top prize for charity.

	Besides Affleck/Ding, Eisenberg/Giamatti, Ritter/Shahi, Scheer/Huebel and Awkwafina/Feig, guests in the hot seat this season have included Larry David & Cazzie David, Jason Alexander & Wayne Knight, Tig Notaro & Pete Holmes, Brad Paisley & Clayton Kershaw, and Michael Kosta & Wendi McLendon-Covey.

	Still to come are Will Forte & Taran Killam, Colin Jost & Michael Che, Michael Keaton & Jon Lovett, Timothy Simons & Jackie Tohn, Billy Porter & Leslie Odom Jr., and Sarah Jane Nader & Brooks Nader. 

	“Who Wants To Be A Millionaire,” from Sony Pictures Television’s Embassy Row and Kimmelot, is executive produced by Michael Davies and Jimmy Kimmel. The series is produced by Sony Pictures Television’s Embassy Row and Kimmelot.

schema.headline: ‘Who Wants to Be a Millionaire’ Ends Summer Run With Consecutive Weeks of Ratings Growth

title: Odyssey Entertainment Group Launches Original Content Division to Collaborate With Creators
description: Nashville-based Odyssey Entertainment Group has launched a division designed to partner with creators to develop content under a model designed to a
body:
Nashville-based Odyssey Entertainment Group has launched a division designed to partner with creators to develop content under a model designed to allow them to own the underlying intellectual property.

	Odyssey Entertainment was formed in 2021 by Nicole Kasper and Paige Kosinski as a management and brand partnership firm to support creators and other artists working across broad verticals such as lifestyle, comedy, food, wellness, business, entertainment, fashion and home. With the launch of Odyssey Originals, the company is expanding into production.
	

	“People over profit has always been one of our company’s main pillars, and Odyssey Originals istaking that to another level,” Kasper said. “Helping someone achieve their dream shouldn’t cost them anything. If we do our job right, they win big, and we grow right alongside them.”


	Said Kosinski, “Our talent will build franchises beyond just their following and own what they make. That’s exactly what legacy over likes looks like in practice.”

	Odyssey Originals will work in tandem with existing production banners King Jester, which focuses on comedy, and SickBird Productions, a female-led firm focused on podcasts, documentaries and digital series.

	Odyssey and SickBird previously teamed on the podcast “You Had 2 Be There,” co-hosted by Odyssey-repped Nicole Story Dent alongside Kate Steinberg and Erin Miller.

	“Building on the momentum of ‘You Had 2 Be There,’ we’re proud to expand our partnership withOdyssey, grounded in a shared belief that the best stories are built through trust, creativeambition, and a creator-first mindset,” said Jade Watson, CEO of SickBird, shared. “The future ofentertainment belongs to creators, but they deserve a model that values both creativity andownership. At SickBird, we believe creator empowerment and exceptional storytelling go hand inhand, and that combination will define the next generation of entertainment.”
	

	Zack Slingsby and Brendan Nardozzi lead King Jester.

	“Comedy has never been more culturally relevant, but great scripted comedy is difficult to find,”said Slingsby. “There are more talented comedians than ever, yet few places built to help themdevelop shows and turn ideas and stories into premium productions. That’s why we built KingJester. Partnering with Odyssey allows us to bring that philosophy to an even broader communityof creators and help develop the next generation of original shows and series.”

	The initial development slate from King Jester include projects with comedians Courtney Michelle, Antonio Baldwin and Kristen Marie.

	“As creators, the projects that we develop become deeply personal. They are our babies. Being able to retain 100% IP is unheard of and its proof of how much Odyssey respects and believes in the talent they work with,” Michelle said.

	(Pictured: Odyssey Entertainment founders Paige Kosinski and Nicole Kasper)

schema.headline: Odyssey Entertainment Group Launches Original Content Division to Collaborate With Creators

title: Jackbox Games Sets ‘Party Pack 12,’ ‘Trivia Murder Party 3’ Releases as CEO Teases New Streaming Service (EXCLUSIVE)
description:
Jackbox Games has unveiled the release dates and trailers for its upcoming “Trivia Murder Party 3″ and “Party Pack 12.”

	“Party Pack 12″ (unveiled
body:
Jackbox Games has unveiled the release dates and trailers for its upcoming “Trivia Murder Party 3″ and “Party Pack 12.”

	“Party Pack 12″ (unveiled in the trailer above) will be available Oct. 15. “Trivia Murder Party 3″ (featured in the announcement video below) will launch Sept. 17. 

	The launches come as Jackbox is experiencing a major moment of validation, with streaming giants including Netflix and Amazon shifting their gaming strategies to focus on casual games — the kind Jackbox has been regularly making since its annual “Party Pack” first released in 2014.
	

	“We consider that somewhat validating of what we do,” Jackbox Games CEO Mike Bilder tells Variety. “We’ve been making these casual, social party games annually since 2014, with an annual release of the ‘Jackbox Party Pack.’”

	Jackbox has partnered with both Netflix (which currently offers a three-game pack called “Jackbox Party Essentials”) and Amazon (which previously had a Jackbox Games subscription channel available on its Luna gaming platform), and Bilder says Jackbox continues to see those platforms and what they are looking to offer as “quite interesting.”



	

	



	“We consider real casual gamers to be our audience. We don’t necessarily consider AAA games to be competition for us,” Bilder says. “Of course, they absorb the dollars spent from people, from gamers, and they also absorb time. But our competition isn’t ‘Fortnite’ or ‘GTA,’ our competition is the game of Life or Clue, or Charades, or ‘Rock Band,’ or something that somebody’s going to play at a party where there’s a couple hours to hang out with friends or family. So we do think getting to very casual audiences is a great strategy for us. So being available on smart TVs and on hardware that people have in their homes that maybe those people don’t consider themselves gamers — they don’t own an Xbox or PlayStation, but they have a smart TV and they know how to download a Netflix or Hulu app.”
	

	Bilder says Jackbox is currently working on its own proprietary “streaming solution” that will launch later this year that allows easy access to Jackbox’s games.

	“We really think that’s an interesting opportunity of expansion and focus,” Bilder says. “And again, I think competition is always interesting. It somewhat validates what you’re doing, but I also think it’s kind of lifting all boats for us, too. And hopefully, there’s more eyeballs and opportunity for folks to find out about Jackbox Games and have a device in their home that they can play about.”



	

					Jackbox Games CEO Mike Bilder; VP of business development Andy Kniaz/Jackbox Games
	



	In addition to playing in a more social and less competitive (skill-wise) genre, Jackbox is offering lower-spec games than its AAA competition. But that isn’t how Jackbox thinks about it.

	“I’d like to replace low spec with accessible because low spec can kind of sound like you’re talking about what a game lacks, and accessibility is really about how many barriers we’ve removed, and I think Jackbox does a lot of things to remove those barriers,” Andy Kniaz, Jackbox’s VP of business development says. “I was reading about this recently, and I know New Zoo, as an example, just came up with this fascinating statistic that I think two-thirds of PC games played last year were played specifically on machines that didn’t require a hardware upgrade. So the games that they were choosing were geared toward the stuff they already had because the cost of upgrading was too cost prohibitive to basically take that on, and I think that that’s pretty amazing. It’s a pretty amazing move to see people understand that value isn’t necessarily just based on how many polygons you’re moving on a screen.”



	

	



	Currently, Jackbox is available across 13 platforms, and as Bilder said, is developing a streaming service for smart TVs. Under Kniaz’s team, Jackbox is also exploring publishing third-party games and has announced its first title in that space, “My Arms Are Longer Now.” 

	But the party-game publisher’s main focus is still its own IP, like “Trivia Murder Party,” which began as an offering in a “Party Pack” and has since spun out into its own franchise due to popularity.

	“It’s really promising to start to see our IP become valuable,” Kniaz says. “When you have Netflix and you can do a business deal and put your IP on Netflix next to all of those named products, I think that really proves where the Jackbox IP is these days. And as Mike is saying, we’re always open to partnership. It just has to line up, and it has to make sense for the games, and it has to make sense for our player.”
	

	The upcoming “Party Pack 12″ includes the below titles.

	• We Forgot a Card (Design, Joke-Writing): A game where you craft ridiculous greeting cards for weird occasions with the option to purchase them IRL. You’re running late to your big event and you stumble upon a shop with limited options. Time to get creative.• MegaPals (Speed, Guessing): A mind-melding game that celebrates friends both old and new. See how connected you are with your pals through impulsive wordsmithing and explosive match-ups. How well do you know how your fellow players think?• Debate and Switch (Presentation, Head-to-Head): A game of dispute and discussion where lighthearted topics meet lively debate. Persuade your fellow players to side with your silly and strongly held opinions in this town hall talk-’em-up tourney.• Idol Factions (Teamwork, Trivia): An action-packed battle of facts where two teams race to sort answers into the right categories. You’ll need to think fast and yell loudly to sort the answers that just keep coming.• Hyperface (Head-to-Head, Photoediting): A game where you take selfies or use stock photos and warp them in wild ways in order to respond to bizarre prompts like “your face when you’ve just seen a bear.” Smudge, yank, squash and draw on photos to create one-of-a-kind masterpieces meant to be shared.The Jackbox Party Pack 12 will be arriving later this year on PC (Steam and Epic Games Store), PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X|S, Nintendo Switch, Switch 2, Apple TV, iPad and the Mac App Store.

title: ‘Insidious: Out of the Further’ Review: Latest Entry in the Franchise Serves Up Genuinely Terrifying Setpieces Despite a Convoluted Final Act
description: If you’ve always been terrified of dental work and the idea of someone poking around your pearly whites with sharp tools, you’re not alone. With “In
body:
If you’ve always been terrified of dental work and the idea of someone poking around your pearly whites with sharp tools, you’re not alone. With “Insidious: Out of the Further,” the sixth entry in the infinitely inventive horror franchise, writer-director Jacob Chase is unashamed to declare that he shares your fears, while having some gross-out fun with this widespread irrational phobia.

	A largely setpiece-driven chapter with a wobbly story but several impeccable vignettes that drill into our deepest bedtime anxieties, “Out of the Further” (like the rest of the films in the series) follows a group of unlucky humans plagued by demonic spirits that live in a dream space called “The Further,” and occasionally travel into the real world to hijack pockets of life and energy. And some of the film’s most impressive frights take place in the dentist’s chair, veering into serious body-horror territory. 
	

	It’s not that Gemma (Amelia Eve), the young single mother and dental hygienist that leads the film, has any sadistic intentions à la “Marathon Man” or “The Dentist,” even though Chase surely had those films in mind to some degree, while slightly flipping the script on them — making the patient, not the provider, the main perpetrator. In one of the most effective scenes, an old man (David Morgan) with rotting teeth, and quite possibly a second set of much sharper fangs, terrorizes and injures Gemma while she scrapes off sizable heaps of slimy residue from his mouth, even pulling out strands of hair as he silently stares at her. (Feel free to either gag along or close your eyes.)
	

	The patient in question is one of a trio of dead people strolling around Gemma’s neighborhood; another is styled in such a hagsploitation manner that it’s impossible not to think of Aunt Gladys from “Weapons.” The entities continually lurk into Gemma’s house and into the eyes of her precocious nine-year-old daughter, Maya (Island Austin), trying to intimidate the family of two. It’s actually curious that Gemma chose to stay in that same house after the events of the terrific opening prologue, set in 1999, in which the young Gemma (Charli Penton, brilliant in a short role) witnesses the brutal death of her fragile mother through an inexplicable series of supernatural happenings. 

	Twenty years later, she wants to be a different kind of mother to her school-obsessed daughter, encouraging her quirks (like her insistence on building little crawl spaces out of couch cushions) and being emotionally present. But her kindly and supportive cop boyfriend Nick (Brandon Perea) rightly insists that the duo should perhaps move out of the house when Gemma’s habitual nightmares intensify. As she goes deeper into the Further in her dreams, she occasionally and unwittingly brings back a spirit or two. But little does Nick know that it is Gemma, and not the house, that is haunted.

	Chase’s script doesn’t spend a lot of time explaining the idea of “The Further” to those unfamiliar with the franchise, the concept is still basic enough to follow: It’s a world that supernaturally gifted people like Gemma travel to while sleeping, crawling with demons, all looking for a living being to latch onto. While Gemma is in the Further, the film unleashes a number of polished horror sequences, the most frightening one turning Maya’s crawlspace into an airless, claustrophobic maze that wouldn’t be out of place in “Backrooms.” With effective sound design and customary jump scares, “Out of the Further” knows exactly what it wants to be for a while: an atmospheric, vibes-based horror film that will make any nervous sleeper check under their bed before turning the lights off. You know, just in case.

	But the story’s shortcomings rise to the surface in due course, especially when Elise (Lin Shaye) — the franchise’s most beloved character, now deceased — re-enters the picture as a ghost who helps people like Gemma find their way back home. In this chapter, Elise communicates to the living via Clare (Maisie Richardson-Sellers), a talented tattoo artist and a selfless medium invested in helping Gemma and Maya get rid of Lester (Joseph Lopez), the main demon who wants to make our world a playground for his kind. A scene where Clare tries to explain Elise’s plan to Gemma, Nick, and Maya using a bunch of cut-up oranges makes so little sense that one wonders if the writers were trying to convince themselves first and foremost that the convoluted scheme is actually quite simple. (It’s far from it.) If the first two (and best) “Insidious” movies have taught us anything, it is that the fear of losing one’s family, and knowing that the only way is out is through, is enough of an emotional terror. While Chase’s film captures that feeling soundly for a while, with both Eve and Austin painting a beautiful mother-daughter portrait, it also makes you wish for a leaner resolution in its later moments.
	

	Still, there is much old-school horror fun to be had here, with costume designer Liz Keogh Palmer and the team of makeup artists especially deserving of credit with their mind-blowing work on various evil spirits. Many of them might just make an appearance in your consciousness when the lights go off.

schema.headline: ‘Insidious: Out of the Further’ Review: Latest Entry in the Franchise Serves Up Genuinely Terrifying Setpieces Despite a Convoluted Final Act

title: Marc Jacobs Says He'd Dress Luigi Mangione For His Murder Trial
description:
Marc Jacobs
                          I'd Happily Style Luigi For Court ...
body:
Marc Jacobs
                          I'd Happily Style Luigi For Court ...
                          But 'Trendsetter' Doesn't Need My Help!!!
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              August 19, 2026
                            9:06 AM PDT
                                                                            
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Marc Jacobs isn't above giving Luigi Mangione a style makeover for his upcoming New York state murder trial ... though he doesn't seem to think Luigi needs his help.
      
    
            The famous fashion designer appeared on an episode of Variety's "Lie Detector Test" series ... when an interviewer brought up the bevy of celebs who have flashed Marc's designs at their court appearances -- including Winona Ryder, Lil Kim and Courtney Love.
      
    
            The interviewer then asked Marc if he'd consider styling Luigi for his upcoming murder trial ... and he said yes.
      
    
            However, when asked how he might improve Luigi's style, he admitted the guy has done a pretty good job dressing himself for court without any help.
      
    
            Marc then agrees that Luigi is a "trendsetter" ... because Nordstrom apparently sold out of the maroon sweater fans believe Luigi wore in court.
      
    
            While Marc might be down to make sure Luigi's dressed to the nines at his state murder trial, he may not get the chance ... because Luigi's defense team is trying to get the case dismissed.
      
    
        
                    
                  
      
    
            As we reported ... Luigi has asked a judge to dismiss the case -- claiming he can't be tried again now that he pled guilty to federal stalking charges and admitted that he killed UnitedHealthcare CEO Brian Thompson.
      
    
            Prosecutors in the case have until early October to argue the trial should proceed ... at the very least delaying the start of his murder trial if it isn't dismissed.
      
    
            If Luigi does have to stand trial in the state case, at least he'll look good doing it!

                          Cops Conduct Death Investigation to Determine if Criminal Conduct Involved

                                  August 19, 2026

            Police are not satisfied Hayden Panettiere's death was a tragic overdose of prescribed meds, because they are trying to determine if there could be criminal conduct behind it.
      
    
            Law enforcement sources involved in the case tell TMZ they are conducting a death investigation to see if some illegality is behind the 36-year-old's death.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            As we reported, the Greenville PD showed up Wednesday morning at the family home of her boyfriend, Brian Hickerson. It would appear police want information from Brian regarding any circumstances that might be connected to Hayden's death.
      

        
                    
                  
      
    
            One law enforcement source tells TMZ ... the death investigation was triggered because Hayden's death was "unexpected," since she was only 36 ... adding the police are doing a parallel investigation with the coroner to determine the cause and manner of death.
      
    
            The autopsy has been completed, and the toxicology results are pending.

title: Tupac Cremated and Smoked by Friends, Relatives After Death
description:
Tupac
                          Smoke Him If You Got Him
body:
Tupac
                          Smoke Him If You Got Him
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              August 19, 2026
                            6:52 AM PDT
                                                                      |
                                                                Updated 
                                  August 19, 2026
                                8:08 AM PDT
                                    
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Suge Knight told us a WILD story about Tupac, and it ends with his ashes being rolled up in a blunt.
      
    
            Suge, who was with Tupac in Vegas when the rapper was shot, tells TMZ ... immediately after Tupac died, his mom wanted him cremated.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Suge says someone put him in touch with a guy, late in the evening, from some sort of funeral home. He asked the guy to cremate Tupac, but the man said he was busy for the next few days.
      

        
                    
                  
      
    
            Suge got the guy's address and went over to the guy's house with 2 bags -- one with $200,000 in cash, and the other with $1 million in cash. Suge offered the guy the bag with the $200K, but he said he wouldn't cremate Tupac that night. So Suge says he upped the ante and offered both bags. He says the guy was staring down $1.2M and agreed to cremate Tupac right then and there.
      
    
            As for what happened to Tupac's ashes, Suge said the rapper's mom had people come to the Vegas hotel room where she was staying, and they rolled his ashes into several blunts and they smoked him.
      
    
            For his part, Suge says he told Tupac's mom he was on probation and felt smoking Tupac might be a violation, so he passed.
      
    
            It's been 30 years since Tupac's death, and his accused killer is currently on trial for murder ... though Suge tells us  Duane "Keefe D" Davis wasn't the only one involved in Tupac's "assassination."
